subject: Request: chronology of delegated merge approvals + keystore handback evidence
messages:
From: Alice Park <security@finovate.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:23:00 -0500
Subject: Evidence request — delegated PR approvals and keystore handback chronology

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this through — our external assessor (AuditCo) has flagged a need to see a concise chronology that ties the delegated PR approval policy to actual merge approvals for the period Jul–Oct 2027, plus any documented handback events for the keystore(s) used in production. Specifically they want: 

- A CSV or table of merged PRs that were approved under delegated approval (PR id, author, approver, timestamp, branch, change description).
- Keystore handback/transfer events (who handed back to operations/security, timestamps, ticket id).
- Any exceptions / temporary allowlists and the justification.

Can Redwood provide a short bundle and a one-paragraph narrative describing the delegated approval guardrails and how handback is recorded? AuditCo would like to close this by next week if possible.

Feel free to route questions to me or Sam at AuditCo (cc'd).

Thanks,
Alice Park
Senior Security Reviewer — Finovate Bank
security@finovate.com

--
Attachment: n/a (initial request)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Alice Park <security@finovate.com>; Sam Patel <external_assessor@auditco.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 11:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Evidence request — delegated PR approvals and keystore handback chronology

Alice / Sam — thanks for the clarity. We're on it. High-level answers first, then we'll pull artifacts: 

- Delegated approvals: we use a documented PR gating policy where specific release engineers are given delegated merge authority for hotfix and release branches. Approvals are tied to GitHub review events and enforced by branch protection + CI gates.
- Keystore handback: production keystore custody changes are recorded via our internal ticketing process (SEC- keys) and an HSM handback CSV is maintained by Security.

I'll coordinate a small bundle: a PR approval snapshot CSV, the keystore-handback log (redacted identifiers where needed), the rotation schedule PDF, and a one-page narrative. Irene will pull the logs and Marissa will compile the CSV. Jonas, please confirm the list of delegated approvers (names + github ids) we should include.

Goal: deliver by Tue, 16 Nov EOD. If that timeline is tight for AuditCo please let me know.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: (to follow) planning notes

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 08:12:04 -0500
Subject: Re: Evidence request — delegated PR approvals and keystore handback chronology

Looping in the exact sources and extraction steps so Marissa can pull a clean artifact: 

Sources: 
- GitHub audit API (org:redwood-inference) — review events + merge commits between 2027-07-01 and 2027-10-31. Fields: PR_ID, title, author_login, approver_login(s), merged_at, target_branch, commit_sha.
- CI gating logs from Circle/Runner — pass/fail, job ids for gated merges (for sample correlation).
- Internal ticketing (Jira SEC- prefix) — keystore handback and rotation events; fields: ticket id, actor, timestamp, handback_type (return/handover/rotation), notes.
- HSM management ledger (security drive) — handback CSV maintained by Ops/Security team.

I will export the HSM ledger for the requested time window and redact any customer-specific key ids; we will keep internal reference ids. I also recommend including a short mapping table between PRs and deploys for a 10-sample subset to show the control.

Attachments I will produce for the bundle:
- keystore-handback-log.csv (redacted IDs)
- rotation-schedule.pdf (policy + upcoming rotations)
- access-review-2027-11-01.csv (access list snapshot)

Marissa — please prepare pr-approval-snapshot.csv and a short README that explains columns and redaction rules. Jonas — confirm delegated approver list and provide github ids; I will include that as a small table in the README.

Irene Choi
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: keystore extraction plan (internal)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; irene_choi@redwood.ai; jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:40:21 -0500
Subject: Re: Evidence request — delegated PR approvals and keystore handback chronology

Team — compiled the artifacts and uploaded them to the evidence folder. Summary of what I attached here (stubs included below):

Attachments (in email stub and in Drive):
- pr-approval-snapshot.csv (CSV, 1.8MB) — columns: pr_id, title, author, approver, merged_at, target_branch, ci_job_id, linked_jira_ticket
- keystore-handback-log.csv (CSV, 48KB) — columns: event_id, ticket_id, actor, action, timestamp, hsm_reference (redacted)
- keystore-rotation-schedule.pdf (PDF, 220KB) — policy + planned rotation dates
- access-review-2027-11-01.csv (CSV, 120KB) — who had keystore access on the sample date

Uploads and links: 
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD_keystore-evidence
- Jira: SEC-8421 is the intake ticket for this bundle (contains links to the full exports).

I sampled 10 PRs that were merged under delegated approval (listed in the CSV) and included CI job ids so the assessor can correlate. I also added a short README in the Drive that explains redaction rules and how to map our internal HSM references to Jira.

If Alice/Sam want us to produce a single PDF bundle we can do that and sign it off.

Marissa Cole
Principal Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: pr-approval-snapshot.csv (CSV), keystore-handback-log.csv (CSV), keystore-rotation-schedule.pdf (PDF), access-review-2027-11-01.csv (CSV)

- What you get: pr-approval-snapshot.csv, keystore-handback-log.csv (redacted), keystore-rotation-schedule.pdf, access-review-2027-11-01.csv, README explaining redactions and mapping.
